final_decision.rationale: Compression ruled out on all 5 pairs (block_boundary 0.997-1.004; unique_G=256; dct_zero 0.015). Blur ruled out (spectral_slope_ratio 0.947-0.986 < 1.08; FFT anisotropy 0.00). Noise is chroma-dominant, YCrCb-space, severity 4 (pair0 sigma 33.85; sim 36.8; sev3 under-shoots to 29.9, sev5 over-shoots to 42.9). Global is luma-preserving YCrCb-space saturation strengthen sev1 (chroma x2): pair-level evidence is decisive — colorful images become vividly saturated with near-zero mean shift (pair1 mean -6.3 with chroma ratio 3.85; pair4 -19.2 with chroma 2.99), which rules out HSV-space saturation (tests darken -45.6/-45.9/-82.9) and flat brightness (constant shift ~-25 across pairs, contradicted by pair1/-6.3). Post-noise saturation reproduces pair0 chroma 11.89 (target 11.61), VR 2.623 (2.614), clip 0.4227 (0.403), mean -23.1 (-25.9), cross 0.30 (0.32); on pair1 it reproduces mean -6.6 (-6.3), VR 4.03 (4.34), chroma 3.73 (3.85), spread 1.83 (1.81), cross 0.38 (0.39). Residual uncertainty: verify_signals sigma over-shoots by 57-68% on supports 1/2/4 (target noise appears weaker on those contents than a homogeneous Gaussian model; possibly content-dependent clipping), and residual-intensity correlation (+0.18 on pair0) is better matched by poisson5+satYCrCb1 (+0.20) which otherwise under-shoots. Noise step can never be LIKELY (verify_signals MATCH/PARTIAL only -> UNCERTAIN per protocol). Support validation verdicts: pair0 PARTIAL, pair1 WEAK, pair2 WEAK, pair3 PARTIAL, pair4 WEAK.

second_order_stats.channel_signature: clean channel means are nearly equal on every pair (max/min = 1.07/1.16/1.12/1.05/1.07) but the target residual channel-std ratio is 1.57/1.70/1.59/1.54/2.07 with G always the lowest channel. This is the YCrCb-space chroma-dominant noise signature (R gets 1.402*sigmaCr, B gets 1.772*sigmaCb, G gets suppressed). Speckle and Poisson are per-RGB-channel intensity-proportional (equal channel scaling) and Gaussian_RGB is channel-equal; all three are contradicted. R0 noise type confirmed.
second_order_stats.target_chroma_std: sum std(Cr)+std(Cb) is nearly constant across pairs: 105.16 / 131.30 / 121.17 / 113.17 / 120.84, while clean chroma std varies 9.06 / 34.07 / 28.40 / 18.02 / 40.47. The chroma field is therefore dominated by a fixed additive chroma-noise field; the chroma_ratio spread (11.61/3.85/4.27/6.28/2.99) is driven by clean content, not by a variable saturation strength. Saturation sev1 (x2, luma-preserving) with noise sev4 reproduces pair0 chroma 11.89 and pair1 3.73.
second_order_stats.residual_intensity_corr: ric = +0.187/+0.022/+0.366/+0.197/+0.057 (all >= 0) whereas additive-Gaussian sims give ric ~ -0.05; target residual magnitude grows with intensity, so a Poisson-like component is plausible (retained as alternative).
second_order_stats.sigma_content_dependence: target sigma is inversely related to clean chroma content: low-chroma pairs 0/3 (clean chroma 9.1/18.0) have sigma 33.85/32.62, while colorful pairs 1/2/4 (chroma 34.1/28.4/40.5) have sigma 25.70/25.70/20.88 (pair4 also has clip 0.470). Gamut clipping of the chroma-noise field on colorful/bright content compresses the measured noise, which explains the sigma overshoot of any fixed-severity additive model on those pairs. This is a measurement/clipping effect, not evidence for a lower severity: sev3 makes VR/mean worse and still leaves sigma +33% on pair1.

reanalysis.threshold_boundary_checks: The control fails only the sigma check on pairs 1/2/4 (+57..+68%) while matching mean/VR/chroma/clip/spread/cross within a few percent. Because sigma was the sole discriminator, it was stress-tested with severity +/-1 (noise sev3, sat sev2) and type alternatives (poisson, gamma). R0's documented pair0/pair1 control verdicts were reproduced in-session (pair0 PARTIAL 3/4; pair1 WEAK 2/4 with identical sigma +62% and VR 9%), so the control baseline is seed-stable.

Rich fingerprints (chroma ratio, clipped fraction, per-channel residual std, ric) additionally computed for finalists to guard against gaming the 4-check verifier.

validation.decision_rule_applied: REQUIRED for CHANGE (noise pipelines): verify_signals WEAK->PARTIAL/MATCH improvement on >=4/5 support pairs, or dominant §B statistical improvement. No candidate meets this: best alternative C4 improves only pair2 and regresses pair0/pair3. §B/rich-fingerprint improvement is real but partial (ric, chroma, channel balance) and does not dominate the aggregate verdicts.

decision.rationale: The R0 control remains the best-supported pipeline. All deterministic steps (compression, blur, brightness/gamma-family, order swap) are ruled out or regress support pairs. The control matches pair0 and pair1 mean/VR/chroma/clip/spread/cross within a few percent and is PARTIAL 3/4 on pairs 0 and 3. Its only systematic deviation is the noise_prior sigma overshoot on pairs 1/2/4 (+57..+68%), which is explained by gamut-clipping compression of a fixed chroma-noise field on colorful/bright content (target clip fraction 0.37-0.47; clean chroma std 28-40 on those pairs), and which no tested severity/saturation/type variant closes without regressing the deterministic statistics. The positive residual-intensity correlation (ric +0.02..+0.37) indicates a possible Poisson component; the Poisson alternatives reproduce ric and pair2 but regress pair0/pair3 and do not reach >=4/5 pair improvement, so they do not warrant a CHANGE. R1 budget: 14 test_candidate.py runs (<=15).
decision.next_round_condition: If a future round is allowed, only test pipelines that keep control-level mean/VR/chroma on pairs 0/1/3 while reducing sigma on pairs 1/2/4; Poisson-family without saturation amplification (e.g. poisson5 + milder global) is the only remaining signal-consistent direction.
